llm.summary: This sleep-story narration skill is mostly coherent, but it asks for broad Beatra account powers and silently self-updates by default, so it needs review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Local file upload is limited to user-selected regular files for clone samples, and endpoint URLs are fixed to Beatra hosts; the remote account permissions are broader than the sleep-story task requires.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Device authorization and local credential storage are disclosed, but the installed client silently checks for and applies package updates by default before ordinary commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions include consent and billing checkpoints, but the bundled client accepts any MCP tool name from the command line, so the documented workflow is not enforced by the client.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists a shared bearer token, installation inventory, registration cache, and updater state under ~/.beatra, and automatic updates can replace package-owned executable files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is short sleep-story speech generation with optional voice cloning, but the authorization scope also covers image, video, music, artifact read/write, wallet spending, task cancellation, and general MCP tools.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing. Use it only if you are comfortable granting Beatra a shared local device token with broad media, artifact, task, and billing-related authority. Consider disabling automatic updates with the documented update command, and revoke the Beatra device authorization from the console when you no longer need the skill.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: the broad OAuth scope and arbitrary MCP tool dispatch exceed what this sleep-story workflow needs, even though no credential theft code was found.
[T03] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: automatic package replacement is disclosed and constrained to fixed Beatra URLs with checksums and rollback, but it is enabled by default and lacks independent release signing in the inspected artifact.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: image, video, music, generic artifact, wallet spending, and task-cancel scopes are not proportionate to a speech-focused skill.
[SDI-2] expected: Downgraded in part: voice read/write access fits the optional voice-cloning workflow, but users should understand it grants authority over voice assets.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded: the credential file is explicitly documented, stored under ~/.beatra, and read for Beatra API calls; I found no artifact-backed evidence that the token is printed, moved to argv, or exfiltrated.
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: uninstall, revocation, and local-state cleanup are documented and user-directed, with conservative handling of shared Beatra state.
[AE1] expected: Overridden: scripts/mcp_client.py was present in the artifact and inspected locally, so the reported partial-inspection signal did not hold for this final review.
